headline: Urban Enclave Daily Access Permits
reservation: Due to its proximity to Montreal, this park strictly enforces daily capacity limits. Entry permits must be purchased online via the Sépaq portal before arrival; once the quota is met, no further visitors—including pedestrians—are permitted entry.

days.title: The Lakes of the Mountain

stops.name: Lac Seigneurial
stops.detail: Follow the easy circular path around the park's largest lake, popular for birdwatching and tranquil forest views.

stops.name: Le Moulin Tea House
stops.detail: Visit this historic mill building located between the lakes, often serving as a resting point for walkers.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; local residential roads can be busy during school hours.
days.note: Swimming is strictly prohibited in all park lakes to protect the fragile ecosystem.

days.title: Orchards and Elevated Views
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Discovery Centre

stops.name: The Historic Orchard
stops.detail: See the apple trees that reflect the region's agricultural heritage, particularly vibrant during the spring blossom.

stops.name: Sentier des Sommets
stops.detail: A slightly more rugged trail offering glimpses of the surrounding Monteregian plains.

days.driving: Minimal driving; most sights are connected by a central trail network.
days.note: Trail conditions can be muddy in the spring; stick to the gravel paths during thaws.

days.title: Winter Trails and Forest Solitude
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Main Entrance

stops.name: Lac des Bouleaux
stops.detail: A quieter secondary lake surrounded by birch trees, ideal for seeing local wildlife away from the main crowds.

stops.name: Grand-Duc Trail
stops.detail: A forested loop named after the Great Horned Owl, showcasing the dense canopy of this urban forest.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes from the town center; parking is concentrated at the main gate.
days.note: In winter, specific trails are reserved exclusively for cross-country skiing or fat-biking.

intel.title: Morning Capacity Issues
intel.text: The main lot often fills before 10 AM on sunny weekends and holidays. Access is denied at the gate once the pre-sold permit quota is reached.

intel.title: Full Urban Connectivity
intel.text: Mobile signal is excellent throughout the park due to its location within the Montreal metropolitan area. Offline maps are generally not required for navigation.

intel.title: Immediate Suburban Services
intel.text: Ample fuel and charging stations are located within two kilometers of the park entrance in Saint-Bruno-de-Montarville. No services exist inside the park gates.

intel.title: Weekday Advantage
intel.text: Visit on Tuesday or Wednesday to avoid the heavy local exercise crowds that frequent the trails after work hours. Early morning offers the best birdwatching.

intel.title: Strict Environmental Rules
intel.text: Dogs and other pets are strictly prohibited in this park to protect the local fauna. Ensure you check the 'Prohibited' list on the official site before bringing equipment.

plan.arrival: Fly into Montreal-Trudeau (YUL), take the A-20 East, and source any needs in Longueuil or Saint-Bruno before reaching the park gates.
plan.vehicle: Any standard vehicle is fine; bike racks are highly recommended as the park is a popular cycling hub from the city.
plan.goldenHour: The shores of Lac Seigneurial offer soft light reflections, though the park closes shortly after sunset.
